text:
cs_jordan: GreenCart reporting recurring 429s + long tail latency after hourly traffic surge. Says dedicated pool didn\u2019t scale fast enough — requests queued ~45-90s. Customer asked for urgent help, attached client-side timeline: https://redwood.example/green-cart/incident-logs (sensitive).

mel: Thanks. Can you paste the customer timeline and any request IDs? What time did the spike start?

cs_jordan: Spike started 2025-02-14T09:12:08Z. They shared these excerpts and a cURL repro. Short version: many client requests get 429 after ~30s, others wait ~1m and then succeed.

aj: Pushing to eng-runtime + SRE. Suspect autoscaler backoff + attach/auth slow path. Did we see imagepull or kube-schedule delays for that tenant?

sre_lina: Pulling autoscaler logs now. At 09:12:09 I see a surge decision; desired=12, current=3. But probes started failing and backoff increased, so successive probe windows delayed scale decisions. Also saw repeated attach auth failures for tenant gc-1234.

eng_runtime_bryan: From runtime metrics: scale decision delta ~34s, kube provisioning ~40s, image pull ~12s. The attach handshake to the dedicated backend returned 403 on first few attempts due to short-lived service-account key rotation. That triggered retries and we fell into an exponential backoff.

ops-bot: ALERT: scaleup-delay detected for tenant=gc-1234, probe_fail_rate=26%, attach_auth_fail=7 events in 1m. Incident ID: INC-1759254321.

mel: Can we get a log snippet?

eng_runtime_bryan: Snippet from autoscaler/runtime logs:

```
autoscaler: time=2025-02-14T09:12:09Z decision=scale_up desired=12 current=3 reason=traffic_surge tenant=gc-1234
provisioner: time=2025-02-14T09:12:13Z create_pod tenant=gc-1234 err=None
attach: time=2025-02-14T09:12:17Z auth_error tenant=gc-1234 status=403 token_expired=true
attach: time=2025-02-14T09:12:27Z retry_attach attempt=2 status=403
attach: time=2025-02-14T09:12:48Z attach_success pod=gc-1234-xx
```

aj: That attach 403s explain why kube-level provisioning isn't the full story: pods were created but attach stalled until auth succeeded, causing requests to queue.

mel: Customer provided repro steps: 
1) blast traffic with the GreenCart hourly job
2) run `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood/v1/infer -d @payload.json` repeatedly
3) watch 429s and gap in successful responses ~30-90s
They repro locally and in our staging with the same tenant config.

aj: Short-term mitigation options: bump min_replicas for the tenant, enable a small warm_pool, or temporarily route their spike to reserved burst capacity. Which should we do now?

sre_lina: I applied an emergency override: `autoscaler.k8s/override-min=5` for gc-1234 to reduce queueing. Will monitor 15m. Also enabled a 2-node warm_pool for the tenant.

cs_jordan: GreenCart approved config changes. After override they report fewer 429s but still see tail latency on a few requests (~15s).

eng_runtime_bryan: For root cause: token rotation race where the service account key expired right at spike. Our attach path retries with stale token until the rotation refresh completes, which blocks attach. Long-term fix: fetch fresh token on attach start and add short-circuit fallback (fetch-and-retry immediately, not exponential backoff). Also add metrics/alert when attach_auth_fail > 5/min.

mel: Action items:
- ENG-RUNTIME: patch attach flow to always refresh token on attach start + immediate retry (owner: @eng_runtime_bryan)
- ENG-SRE: create alert for attach_auth_fail and probe_fail_rate thresholds (owner: @sre_lina)
- CS: document repro and provide guidance to customers on temporary min_replicas bump (owner: @cs_jordan)
- OPERATIONS: evaluate warm_pool defaults for high-throughput tenants (owner: ops)

aj: I'll open a tracking ticket S-4567 and link logs, timeline, and mitigation steps.

oncall: ack. I'll keep monitoring GC-1234 for 60m and will escalate if attach_auth_fail recurs.

mel: Thanks everyone. Reopen if we see more 429s after warm pool drains.

cs_jordan: Noted. I'll follow up with GreenCart and close the CS loop once stable.
